endorsements.quote: Pre-deployment evidence should include prospective silent-mode or simulation testing in the intended workflow, comparing trigger and handoff decisions with expert adjudication while measuring downstream workload and time to action.
The minimal audit trail supports reconstruction of high-risk interactions while limiting retained data.
Unexplained flows or safety-relevant regressions should trigger staged release, investigation, or rollback under a prespecified policy.

Within each dimension, deployment evidence should de fine the intended population and workflow, classify task risk, prespecify acceptance criteria, and describe degraded oper ation and post-release monitoring.
We should measure missed escalations and avoidable escalations.
Local clinical review should set these thresholds, and post-release monitoring should measure both missed and avoidable escalations.
Evaluation should report outcome gaps across groups, safety-trigger parity, and accessibility success rate.

When these fields are absent, ambiguous, or contradictory, the assistant should label affected claims as insufficiently supported and then request missing information, retrieve a more recent source when available, or escalate according to risk.
Low-risk, evidence-anchored education can be provided autonomously.

unlisted_practices: Evaluate consumer AI health assistants as stateful systems across a multi-session patient journey rather than on isolated prompts and answers.
Bind every material claim to a structured evidence anchor specifying patient, source, date or time window, unit, and source version.
Test correction persistence so that user corrections update shared journey state and persist across later sessions.
Distinguish input-data failures from assistant failures in each stress-test report.
Use protocolized stress tests that vary one stressor at a time, such as missing data, source conflict, language, role, or forced tool use.
Run deterministic safety checks synchronously and reserve expensive adjudication or human review for high-risk or unresolved cases, with defined timeout fallbacks.

Test privacy controls with adversarial consent-transition tests involving shared devices, caregivers, stale sessions, and access after revocation, and ensure revocation propagates across interfaces and stored state.
Require structured handoff notes for escalations, with a staffed destination, receipt confirmation, and fallback when no one accepts the handoff.

Test personalization with counterfactuals that hold clinical facts constant while varying goals, role, literacy, cost, and demographics, and fall back to a safe nonpersonalized policy when goals are missing or conflict.

Evaluate performance across intersecting language, literacy, disability, device, and connectivity subgroups, narrowing intended use and activating an alternative channel when below disparity tolerances.
Maintain a data-flow map covering inputs, tools, storage, telemetry, versions, and vendor chain, and have governance approve secondary uses and independent auditors verify actual flows.
Track over-reliance, dependence, and anxiety signals in pilots with prespecified stopping and escalation rules.

screen.reason: This is a Perspective article that proposes an evaluation and governance framework (journey-level evaluation, stress testing, and deployment requirements) for consumer AI health assistants.
